protocol.name: treeland_output_uuid_unstable_v1
protocol.copyright: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2024 - 2026 UnionTech Software Technology Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
protocol.description:
This protocol lets clients obtain a stable uuid for each output, identifying the physical output device behind it. The uuid is an opaque, non-empty UTF-8 string that remains stable across sessions and output reconnections, so clients and the compositor can persist per-output settings and restore them after a restart. Other treeland protocols, such as treeland_output_manager_v2 and treeland_output_mirror_group_v1, address outputs by these uuids.
The uuid is unique among the currently connected outputs: the compositor must ensure that no two connected outputs report the same uuid at the same time. The compositor derives the uuid from the persistent identity of the device, for example the make, model, and serial reported in its EDID. When no persistent device identity is available, the compositor may derive the uuid from the connector; such a uuid is only stable while the device remains connected to the same connector.
Clients obtain a uuid for a wl_output object via get_uuid on this protocol. A companion protocol, treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1, provides the same uuid for a zwlr_output_head_v1 object; both entry points return the same uuid for the same physical output device. The wlr-output-management head is advertised even while the output is disabled, so the head variant lets clients identify an output that has no live wl_output global; get_uuid is more convenient when the client already holds a wl_output.
Clients must treat the uuid as opaque: they must not parse it, derive meaning from its contents, or present it to users.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1

description.summary: factory for output uuid objects from wl_output

interface.description:
A singleton global that creates treeland_output_uuid_v1 objects from wl_output objects.
The client binds wl_output globals through the wl_registry, then calls get_uuid for each output it wants to identify. The compositor reports the uuid in the initial uuid event on the returned object.
Multiple uuid objects may be created for the same output at the same time; each object reports the uuid independently.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1 object and release the client's binding to the manager global.
Existing treeland_output_uuid_v1 objects created through this manager are not affected and must be destroyed separately by the client.

request.name: get_uuid

description.summary: create a uuid object for a wl_output

request.description:
Create a treeland_output_uuid_v1 object for the given wl_output. The output may be in any state, including disabled: the uuid identifies the physical device regardless of its enabled state. The compositor emits the initial uuid event on the new object immediately after this request.
The output must be a live wl_output resource. An invalid or destroyed object id, or an object of another type, is rejected by the core protocol (wl_display.invalid_object).
For an output that is currently disabled and has no live wl_output global, the client should use the companion treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol with the corresponding zwlr_output_head_v1 instead.

interface.name: treeland_output_uuid_v1
interface.description:
Represents the uuid identity of the output it was created for, obtained from treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1.get_uuid or from the companion treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol. The compositor emits the uuid event once immediately after the object is created, and again whenever the uuid of the output changes, for example when a persistent device identity becomes available after an initial connector-based fallback.
The object is not tied to the lifetime of the wl_output global: when the output is unplugged and its wl_output global is destroyed, this object remains valid and the last reported uuid remains the identity of the physical device, which may reappear later with the same uuid. The client should destroy this object when it no longer needs the mapping.
Note, because treeland_output_uuid_v1 objects are created from multiple independent factory interfaces — treeland_output_uuid_manager_v1 on this protocol and treeland_output_uuid_head_manager_v1 on the companion treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol — the treeland_output_uuid_v1 interface is frozen at version 1.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy this treeland_output_uuid_v1 object. Only this object is affected; the uuid of the output itself does not change, and other objects, including other uuid objects for the same output, are not affected.

event.name: uuid
event.description: Reports the current uuid of the output. It is emitted once immediately after the object is created, and again whenever the compositor determines a different uuid for the output.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: opaque uuid identifying the physical output
